criteria.rationale: The deliverable accurately reflects all order details, item weights, quantities, and shipping method rules from the source documents, and properly resolves the rate conflict in favor of the operative approved record. Specifically, while Shipping parameters.xlsx, working-notes.txt, and record-22.txt list a USD 110 freight flat rate, registry.txt establishes that record-22.txt (revision 3) is an unapproved draft whereas record-17.txt (revision 2, specifying USD 150) is approved and in force. The workbook applies the operative USD 150 freight cost for Pick Ticket B-5005, computes all weights, costs, and savings without arithmetic error (total cost USD 230.95, total industry average USD 312.94, total savings USD 81.99), and refrains from inventing missing tracking numbers or confirmed shipment dates.

evidence.source_quote:
record-17.txt: revision 2; approved 2025-06-20; status in force; approved by process owner.
record-22.txt: revision 3; created 2025-06-23; status draft; not approved.
The registry, not recency alone, determines which record is operative.
evidence.output_quote: Use USD 150, not USD 110. Revision 2 is approved and in force; revision 3 is an unapproved draft. The USD 110 figure in the attachment and working notes does not supersede the approved rate.

evidence.source_quote: Freight flat rate per qualifying shipment: USD 150. Industry average: USD 225. This rate is independent of weight within this category.

criteria.counterevidence: Competing sources attachment:Shipping parameters.xlsx ('flat rate $110'), attachment:working-notes.txt ('Copied on 2025-06-23 from a revision-3 proposal. Freight flat rate per qualifying shipment: USD 110.'), and workspace:record-22.txt ('Freight flat rate per qualifying shipment: USD 110.') give a lower freight rate, but workspace:registry.txt explicitly marks revision 3 (record-22.txt) as an unapproved draft and revision 2 (record-17.txt, USD 150) as approved and in force, which governs per the request instructions.

criteria.rationale: The delivered Excel workbook fulfills all requirements of the prompt for the Shipping Clerk role and Sales department audience. It populates the Daily Shipment Manifest template with all three orders from Pick Tickets 062525.xlsx (A-1001, B-5005, and C-2001), selects the appropriate shipping methods by weight (UPS for 2.5 lbs, Freight for 250 lbs, and Fed Ex for 50 lbs), uses dynamic formulas for weights, row-level savings, and summary totals, and includes a second sheet documenting the basis, rate conflict resolution, recommendations, and unresolved assumptions without unnecessary holds.
